extracted.intended_audience: aspiring sketch comedy writers, comedy teams, and performers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing short, self-contained sketch-comedy scenes emphasizing a single comedic premise (the "game"), its heightening through beats, and a satisfying button. Covers structure, premise development, types of sketches, and an explicit evaluation checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup / Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer audience questions ASAP. Typically 5 lines of dialogue or less. Establish the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quickly give the minimal facts the audience needs to understand the scene (who, where, stakes). Keep exposition short (about five lines or fewer) so the sketch can move quickly to the premise/game.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce the Premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up reality of your world. Add ONE crazy/wacky/funny thing. This is the engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly establish the single unexpected element that will drive the jokes — no multiple competing premises. Present the premise as a normal-seeming reality with one twist.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Game / Middle Section
rubrics_metrics.description: 95% of length comes here. Best jokes are here. Heightening of the game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the middle to explore and escalate the game with the strongest jokes. This is where you develop repeatable moves or patterns that build comedic momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Button / Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Goofiest, most fun part. Final joke that lands the sketch. Leave them laughing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End on the biggest payoff — a final, clear joke that resolves or caps the game. The button should feel inevitable but still surprising and be the funniest moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beats and Heightening
rubrics_metrics.description: 3 beats heighten the game until you reach a breaking point. Each beat: more ridiculous, more specific, more-er.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure escalation as setup → reinforcement → absurd climax. Each beat should escalate the stakes, specificity, or ridiculousness of the game; aim for at least three clear heightening moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a nugget of an idea. Phrase it as 'What if?' This becomes the game of the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn a core 'what if' into concrete game moves; generate escalating answers to the 'what if' question to populate beats and jokes. Use the core question to keep the sketch focused and avoid tangents.

rubrics_metrics.name: What a Sketch Is
rubrics_metrics.description: A short, self-contained scene focused on one unusual thing that heightens to comedic absurdity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the sketch as a single-unit experiment: one world + one unusual premise + escalating comedic responses. If the scene introduces another unrelated unusual thing, it likely has multiple premises and should be split.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big Challenge: Sustaining Tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustain tension between reality and absurdity over several minutes WITHOUT shifting to a new premise OR becoming predictable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the audience anchored in the scene's reality while increasing the absurdity; avoid resetting the premise or changing rules mid-sketch. Vary beats enough to avoid predictability while remaining consistent with the game's logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Sketch Structure – Heightening sketch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best for premises that naturally support iterative escalation; each beat should increase the stakes or absurdity in a clear, connected way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Sketch Structure – Reveal sketch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use constrained information and misdirection so the final reveal reframes earlier beats. Maintain the single premise while guiding the audience toward the payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Sketch Structure – List sketch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series of related items or examples can be comedic through contrast, escalation, or absurd pattern recognition; often relies on rhythm and punchline density rather than a single narrative arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Sketch Structure – Character sketch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy arises from the character's fixed traits interacting with circumstances; ensure the character's rules stay consistent so the game can heighten.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Sketch Structure – Parody sketch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Play off audience expectations of the source format, then introduce the unusual element (the game) that subverts or escalates those conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric question: Is there one unusual thing (clear game)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: does the sketch center on a single, clear comedic game?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for a singular premise that drives the jokes; multiple competing unusual elements indicate multiple premises and weaken focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric question: Does each beat heighten?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: do successive beats escalate the premise in specificity, stakes, or absurdity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each beat makes the situation more extreme or specific than the last, moving toward a climax rather than repeating the same gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric question: Is the button satisfying?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: does the final joke land and provide a clear payoff?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The button should be both the funniest and the most conclusive moment of the sketch; it should feel earned by prior beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric question: Does it sustain without losing the premise?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: does the sketch maintain the original premise throughout without shifting to a new one?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for mid-sketch pivots to new premises or rules — these dilute the game's power. Sustained escalation within the same premise is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric question: Is the world established quickly enough?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: is the necessary setting/context given early so the audience understands the stakes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the audience is left asking basic questions too long, jokes will not land. Aim to answer essential who/where/what questions immediately in the setup.
